cases.name: whole-page-unrotated
cases.covers: The dominant case, and the one every other is a deviation from.

cases.name: whole-page-scaled-up
cases.covers: A scale above one, where rounding can push a dimension either way.

cases.name: whole-page-scaled-down
cases.covers: A scale below one.

cases.name: scale-that-rounds-to-half-a-pixel
cases.covers: A scale chosen so both dimensions land on .5 and the rounding rule shows.

cases.name: scale-so-small-the-page-is-one-pixel
cases.covers: Both dimensions clamp to one rather than to zero.

cases.name: whole-page-rotated-90
cases.covers: A quarter turn swaps width for height.

cases.name: whole-page-rotated-180
cases.covers: A half turn keeps the size and negates the matrix.

cases.name: whole-page-rotated-270
cases.covers: The other quarter turn, which is not the 90 matrix negated.

cases.name: width-viewport-unrotated
cases.covers: An exact width, with height from the aspect ratio.

cases.name: width-viewport-rotated-90
cases.covers: The same width against the swapped aspect ratio.

cases.name: width-viewport-fractional
cases.covers: A width that does not round to itself.

cases.name: width-viewport-of-one
cases.covers: The narrowest request, where the height ratio also collapses.

cases.name: top-left-quadrant
cases.covers: A region whose display-space bottom is not zero.

cases.name: bottom-right-quadrant
cases.covers: The opposite corner, so a sign error cannot pass both.

cases.name: centre-strip-rotated-90
cases.covers: An off-origin region under a quarter turn, which is where the two get confused.

cases.name: centre-strip-rotated-270
cases.covers: The same region the other way round.

cases.name: sub-rect-with-a-width-viewport
cases.covers: A width viewport applied to a region rather than the page.

cases.name: region-taller-than-it-is-wide
cases.covers: A width viewport on a narrow region, where the height multiplies up.

cases.name: fractional-rect-bounds
cases.covers: PDF boxes are not integers, and the matrix must not assume they are.

cases.name: region-flush-with-the-page-top
cases.covers: Display-space bottom of exactly zero, which is the flip boundary.
